cap_ClWeek.text:
Capabilities: week-grid, two-time-zones, work-package-bars, meeting-work-package-chip, context-panel, drag-to-change-dates.
What you see: The week of 12 to 18 October in the calm grid: CEST and UTC columns, soft meetings, a faded past event, Thursday's rollout review dashed because it is not answered yet, BUG #58231 with grab handles in the all-day strip, and the context panel with the next meeting, this week's due work packages and the shortcuts.

cap_ClEvent.text:
Capabilities: event-panel, mail-origin, accept-maybe-decline, linked-work-package, log-time.
What you see: The Thursday rollout review selected. The navigation folds to the rail and the right column shows the event: time, Join, the attendees, the mail the invitation came from, Accept as the one green action, FEATURE #58412 and Log time on this work package with 1 h filled in.

cap_ClMonth.text:
Capabilities: month-grid, work-package-bars, milestone, new-from-empty-day, context-panel.
What you see: October 2026 into November with plain day numbers and today in a filled badge. EPIC #57990 and FEATURE #58412 span their weeks as soft bars, the Go-live Lyon milestone is a diamond on 2 November, and the hovered 28 October offers New meeting and New work package.

cap_ClPlan.text:
Capabilities: work-package-list, grouped-by-status, assigned-to-me-filter, drag-to-block-time, linked-time-block.
What you see: The week with the work package list open beside the grid, grouped by status. TASK #58455 is lifted over Tuesday with a dashed target block from 14:00 to 16:00 and the hint Drop to block time for this work package.

cap_ClLinkWorkPackage.text:
Capabilities: work-package-picker, suggestions-by-reason, event-link-scope, repeating-event-scope, comment-in-activity, work-package-from-event.
What you see: Level 2, act. The navigation folded to the rail, Tuesday's Demo preparation Malmo Energi selected in the week, and on the right a 440 px panel Link to work package with the same picker as in mail: the field empty and the suggestions Mentioned in this event, Same people and Recent. Under it the scope This event or This and following events, one checkbox to post a comment, the green Link and New work package from this event.

cap_ClEventPopover.text:
Capabilities: events-create-drag, events-popover-editor, events-editor-upgrade, events-title, events-times, events-all-day, events-pick-calendar, avail-drag-teammate.
What you see: A time range dragged out on Tuesday 14:00 to 15:00 as a dashed ghost, and beside it the quick popover with title, start and end, the All day switch and the calendar chooser open, which also lists Tom Achterberg under Delegated to you. On Monday Tom's name is being dropped from the calendar list onto 12:00 to plan a one-to-one.

cap_ClEventEditor.text:
Capabilities: events-full-editor, events-multi-day, events-separate-tz, events-converted-tz, events-rich-description, events-status, events-own-colour, events-categories.
What you see: The navigation folded to the rail and the full editor as a 440 px panel beside the grid: type switch, title, a two day event with a time zone per end and the converted local time under each, location, a formatted description, status, own colour, categories with suggestions and a new one typed, availability and visibility, and the unsaved changes bar at the bottom.

cap_ClEventExtras.text:
Capabilities: remind-add, remind-fixed, remind-keep-foreign, events-attach-file, events-open-attachment, events-attachment-access, integ-talk-new, integ-zoom.
What you see: The same editor scrolled down: four reminders of different kinds, each with its notification or email choice and a remove button, the attachments with Choose from Files and Upload from this device, the outside link confirmation and the question whether invitees get access, and the video call section with a new or existing Talk conversation, where the link goes, Meet and Teams, and Connect Zoom.

cap_ClCalendarEdit.text:
Capabilities: setup-rename-calendar, setup-calendar-colour, setup-delete-calendar, setup-never-busy, remind-default-calendar, avail-block-auto, share-edit-confidential, share-publish.
What you see: The dialog of the calendar Northwind team in four frames: the details with name, colour, what it holds, never busy, Also keep busy in Personal, default reminders and video call, export, and Delete this calendar at the bottom left of the footer; the countdown after that button, where the footer makes way for Cancel the deletion; the sharing part with a person, a group, a team and someone on another server, each with Can edit and Sees private events, and under Links the private link for another app and the public link with its switch, copy subscription link, copy embed code and send by mail; and the same dialog for a calendar Tom shared with you, with Remove from my list. Both tabs end in Cancel and Save.

cap_ClAddCalendar.text:
Capabilities: setup-create-calendar, setup-create-task-calendar, setup-holiday-calendar, setup-subscribe-link, avail-pin-teammate, share-delegated-view, impexp-multi, impexp-result.
What you see: Add calendar as a dialog with the eight ways down the left and Import open: three dropped calendar files with a target calendar per file, one of them a new calendar, and the result with how many events came in and how many failed. A second frame shows the other seven ways as they open on the right: new calendar with or without a task list, holidays by region, subscribe from a link, the administrator's suggestions, the calendars you follow in your mail account, a colleague found by email with Show until I close it and Add to my list, calendars delegated to you grouped per person, and Import before any file is dropped.

cap_ClPublicCalendar.text:
Capabilities: share-public-view, share-multi-public, share-public-readonly, share-public-subscribe, search-public-filter, events-read-only, integ-embed-live.
What you see: Two published calendars of Northwind Projects on one public page without the app frame: the month with both colours, the view menu open, a text filter on review with the line 2 of 24 events match, Subscribe (stays up to date) and Download .ics (a copy of today), and the Thursday rollout review open read only in the right panel. Under it an inset of the same calendar embedded live on the organisation's website.

cap_ClBookingPage.text:
Capabilities: avail-person-page, avail-pick-date, avail-booking-timezone, avail-book-no-account, avail-slot-taken, avail-confirm-email, avail-reschedule-link.
What you see: Olivia Brandt's booking page as a visitor sees it: her three public schedules, the 30 minute introduction chosen, Wednesday 14 October picked in the month, six open slots in a chosen time zone, and the form with name, email address and a note. Four small frames beside it: the slot was taken meanwhile, check your mail and confirm within 24 hours, the page behind the confirmation link with the two choices Reschedule and Cancel the appointment, and the reason with the one red button after Cancel is chosen.

cap_ClFindTime.text:
Capabilities: avail-freebusy-grid, avail-suggest-slots, avail-apply-slot, avail-ooo-tentative, avail-local-time, rooms-browse, rooms-filter-building, rooms-status.
What you see: A wide dialog over the dimmed event: a day grid of five attendees and three rooms with busy, tentative and out of office drawn apart, each person's local time, a suggested row where everyone is free and 14:00 picked, and on the right the room picker with search, building and equipment filters, Lyon, Kassel and Malmö as cards, Kassel warned as no longer free. Frame b opens the same grid from a contact menu.

cap_ClScheduling.text:
Capabilities: avail-copy-link, avail-schedule-duplicate, avail-schedule-delete, avail-oneoff-drag, avail-custom-url, avail-link-expiry, avail-shared-link, avail-booking-written.
What you see: The Scheduling page with the appointment schedules, one-off links, open meeting proposals and the bookings that came in, each already on the calendar with the booker as attendee. On the right a one-off link being made: three times dragged on a mini week, a custom address, an expiry date and whether one or several people can book.

cap_ClScheduleEditor.text:
Capabilities: avail-schedule-edit, avail-booking-video, avail-slot-length, avail-hours-weekday, avail-prep-time, avail-booking-window, avail-conflict-calendars, integ-profile-action.
What you see: The schedule dialog over the dimmed Scheduling page in two columns: name, description, location and the video room switch, length and step, bookable hours per weekday with two ranges on Monday, preparation and follow-up time, the booking window and daily cap, the calendars that take bookings and hide clashes, and the visibility with the profile action Schedule an appointment.

cap_ClProposal.text:
Capabilities: avail-proposal-grid, avail-proposal-length, avail-proposal-participants, integ-talk-proposal, avail-proposal-tentative, avail-vote-matrix, avail-proposal-decide, avail-vote-timezone.
What you see: The week with the busy time of participants hatched and three candidate times held as dashed tentative entries, Thursday 10:00 chosen. The right panel has the title, length presets, participants marked required or optional, the Talk switch and the vote matrix with one button that makes the event. Frame b is the plain voting page Marc Dubois sees without an account, with a time zone picker.

cap_ClRepeat.text:
Capabilities: recur-every-n, recur-weekly, recur-monthly-nth, recur-yearly-day, recur-end, recur-sentence, recur-unsupported-warning, recur-change-future.
What you see: The repeat dialog for the daily stand-up over the dimmed week: Repeat every 1 weeks, Monday to Friday pressed, the end never, on a date or after a number of times, and the rule as one sentence. Below it the monthly and yearly forms, Priya's birthday set from her contact card, a Microsoft 365 series with a rule that is not fully supported, and the two small questions after a change or a delete: only this event, this and following, or all events.

cap_ClAttendees.text:
Capabilities: invite-add-people, invite-group, invite-team, invite-no-forward, invite-roles, invite-status-counts, invite-answer-series, invite-attendee-warning.
What you see: As organiser of the scope review the people section with the count of answers, the switch that stops forwarding, Marc delegated to Lea Fontaine, and his row menu open with role, reply requested, send an email, make organiser and remove. Beside it the search that finds contacts, a contact group and a team, the attendee side of Tom's invitation with a note, the notes of others and which calendar answers, the state where everyone declined, and the line that asks for an email address first.

cap_ClEventMenu.text:
Capabilities: events-drag-move, events-drag-resize, events-multi-drag, events-multi-colour, avail-block-selected, avail-block-visibility, avail-block-status, invite-delete-note.
What you see: Two events selected and dragged together three hours later, ghosts at their old time, the lifted block with its new time and a resize handle on its lower edge, and the context panel that lists where each is blocked. Below it the menu of the two selected events with Block on another calendar open, and the delete dialog for an invitation with a note to the organiser.

cap_ClSettingsCalendars.text:
Capabilities: default-calendars, birthday-calendar, attachment-folder, connected-accounts, profile-and-account, delegates, caldav-addresses, trash-bin.
What you see: The settings dialog in three frames. Defaults and accounts over the dimmed week: the defaults for new events and invitations with Saved beside a changed row, the birthday calendar and the attachment folder, Google and Microsoft 365 connected with Disconnect and buttons to connect Google, iCloud or Microsoft, one link Manage your account in the workspace, and the two addresses for other calendar apps in full, labelled by device, with Copy. Then the same dialog on Sharing and delegates with two delegates, Revoke and Add delegate and the line how to share one calendar only, and on Trash bin with Restore, Delete for good, Empty trash and the 30 day line.

cap_ClSettingsView.text:
Capabilities: theme-and-scale, language-and-region, week-start-time-format, grid-switches, month-limit-slot-size, editor-choice, maps-app, time-zones.
What you see: The settings dialog on View: theme, interface scale, language and region, marked as applying to all apps, week start and time format; the grid switches for weekends (Saved), week numbers and declined events, the month limit, slot size, whether a click opens the quick popover or the full editor, and the maps app; then the time zones with the UTC warning, browser or fixed zone, the switch prompt, the button Show another time zone for now with the key Z, and the shown zones CEST and UTC with the arrows, Make primary and a row menu open with Rename, Replace with another zone and Remove.

cap_ClSettingsReminders.text:
Capabilities: default-reminders, notification-sound, invitation-notifications, desktop-browser-notifications, side-panel-lead.
What you see: The settings dialog on Reminders and notifications: the default reminder for timed and all-day events with Saved beside the changed one, the notification sound with a play button, the invitation and desktop switches with the browser permission state, and how long before a meeting it shows in the side panel. Working hours and video calls live under Scheduling.

cap_ClAdmin.text:
Capabilities: admin-defaults, recommended-public-calendars, who-may-use, outside-accounts, block-external-invitations, force-reminder-kind, booking-subscriptions-export.
What you see: The calendar page in the administration, Ines Okafor in the header and ClAdminNav on Settings: defaults for everyone (view, weekends, reminder, time zone, quick popover or full editor), the three calendars Suggested by your administrator with their subscriber counts and Add public calendar, and the access and limits card with who may use the calendar and Change groups, outside accounts, blocking invitations outside the organisation, the kind of reminder users may add, appointment schedules, subscriptions from a link and export of single events, with Save changes and Discard changes at the bottom.

cap_ClYear.text:
Capabilities: views-year, views-day, views-days-shown, views-month-list, views-click-day-number, views-collapse-allday, views-next-event, setup-upcoming-panel.
What you see: 2026 as twelve small months with week numbers and a dot on each day that has events, the panel Coming up at the right with Earlier and Later (hovered, with its tooltip) and the calendar chooser; a second frame with the view menu open: day, a chosen number of days with its stepper on the row, week, month, year and the agenda list that replaces the panel, and the all day switch greyed because it does not apply to the year view.

cap_ClCommandMenu.text:
Capabilities: search-command-menu, a11y-key-list, a11y-key-navigate, a11y-key-event-actions, views-legend, views-status-styling, events-cancelled-mark, remind-bell.
What you see: The command menu opened with Ctrl K over the week, with actions, go to and settings each with their key and the hint Enter runs or switches, while the grid shows a free, a tentative and a cancelled event, your own unanswered, maybe and declined invitations, bells for reminders, a ticked task at 100% and a task card from a board on its due date; the side panel is the one of every screen. A second frame shows the shortcut overview opened with ?, every shortcut in groups and the legend that explains each style.

cap_ClPhone.text:
Capabilities: mob-answer, mob-timezone, mob-create-edit.
What you see: Five phone frames: the day list with UTC named once per day under the first start, the same list with the Show times in menu open, the Lyon rollout invitation with Accept, Maybe and Decline as a bar at the bottom, the event form as a full screen sheet with title, time, calendar, people, work package and reminder, and the More menu of the invitation as a sheet with Edit my copy.

cap_ClWorkPackageCalendar.text:
Capabilities: integ-workspaces, tasks-pick-props, tasks-filter-view, tasks-add-view, tasks-remove-view, tasks-edit-props, tasks-move-item.
What you see: Two frames. The OpenProject panel beside the week: one row per linked project with its selections under it (Work package dates, Milestones), a switch each, Link another project, and the selected selection with the date it uses, its status, type and date filters, Add another selection from this project and Remove this selection; the navigation shows the same list. Then FEATURE #58412 opened from its bar in the all-day strip into a popover that edits subject, dates, status, assignee and project, with Open in OpenProject.

cap_ClSettingsScheduling.text:
Capabilities: working-hours, custom-video-service.
What you see: The settings dialog on Scheduling: the working hours per weekday with a switch per day and the hours as ranges that are changed in place, the line that Find a time uses them, and the video call services in one table: Talk, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Zoom and Northwind Jitsi as a fixed link of another service, with Add service.
